name: Friedrich Engels
role: German philosopher, revolutionary socialist and co-founder of Marxism (1820-1895)
summary: Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx and, in works such as Anti-Dühring, Socialism: Utopian and Scientific and The Origin of the Family, set out a materialist account of history, class struggle, the state as a class instrument and a planned classless society that would abolish private property, money and religion's social basis. He favoured a democratic republic, universal suffrage and an independent workers' party, while holding revolution justified and defending the Paris Commune as the dictatorship of the proletariat; late in life he stressed mass electoral organisation over minority uprisings.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Proposed a state-capital national bank with all private banks suppressed, so money would not be left to the market.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stated that the division of labour as known will completely disappear, with people moving between branches of production.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Called for abolishing the survivals of feudalism and absolutism and, in 1848, all baronial estates and feudal burdens.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Said relations between the sexes become a purely private matter into which society has no occasion to intervene, though monogamy would be realised.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Said that once all production is in the nation's hands money becomes superfluous and wage labour disappears with the proletariat.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Argued against making every worker owner of a dwelling as a Proudhonist remedy; the shortage would be relieved by requisitioning luxury housing, not by universal ownership.

alienated-labor.rationale: Described workers reduced to one-sided, repetitive tasks and subordinated to a single branch of production, a condition communism would end.

ban-cartels.rationale: Saw trusts as a step toward socialised production and state takeover; treated competition itself as a fetter, so breaking up monopolies to restore competition is opposite to his aim.

bound-labor.rationale: Demanded abolition without compensation of all feudal burdens, labour services and tithes on the peasantry.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Criticised the imperial constitution because chambers could not reject taxes, treating that as a key power; also noted it as a bourgeois lever.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Said capitalism's crises recur and cannot be abolished within it, but in 1895 admitted that 1848 hopes of imminent collapse were mistaken and capitalism still had room to expand.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Predicted that the competition in armaments among great states would end in a general war that would ruin the old order, linking it to the existing order, not to capitalism as such.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Wrote that the bourgeoisie played a most revolutionary part historically and created the productive forces that make a classless society possible.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wanted credit centralised in a state bank run in the interests of the whole people, not independent of the government.

central-planning.rationale: Wanted production by the whole of society according to a definite plan, replacing the anarchy of competing producers.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mixed: 1849 praised US conquest of California as civilising; in 1882 said colonies would be taken over temporarily by the proletariat and led to independence, forcing no blessings.

class-collaboration.rationale: Opposed bourgeois socialists who want to keep society while removing its evils and insisted communists struggle against them.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Wrote that the history of all existing society is the history of class struggles, and in 1879 reaffirmed class struggle as the immediate driving force of history.

collective-farming.rationale: Proposed that large estates become state property worked on a large scale, and that small peasants be led voluntarily into cooperatives, not forced.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Said colonies of native populations should be led toward independence and a victorious proletariat cannot conduct colonial wars.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Called struggle for existence one-sided as a model for history and held that cooperation matters; class struggle, not individual competition, drives history.

conscription.rationale: Backed universal liability for short-term military service in a militia-style army (two years' service) against a long-service professional army.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Demanded abolition of all indirect state and local taxes and, in 1848, abolition of taxes on consumption.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Condemned the New Poor Law of 1834 as cruel and as embittering the poor; blamed pauperism on the economic system, not on relief.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Argued German socialists should defend against Russia in a war and fight it by revolutionary methods, not seek their own side's defeat.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Wrote that the Paris Commune was the dictatorship of the proletariat and told critics to look at it; called the democratic republic its specific form.

direct-action.rationale: In 1895 urged using universal suffrage and elections to grow the party and said barricade-style minority actions were obsolete.

direct-votes.rationale: Accepted the draft's demand for the people's right to propose and reject laws with clearer wording, while calling direct legislation something the party could ultimately do without.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Said a socialist Germany must let the populations of North Schleswig and Alsace-Lorraine decide freely where they belong.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Expected production to expand until it satisfies the needs of all members of society; distribution by common agreement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Held that the party could come to power only under a democratic republic and attacked the monarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Proposed equal rights and equal duties for all as the programme demand, while calling formal equality a historical product.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said the real proletarian content of equality is abolition of classes and that demands for equality beyond that become absurd; also proposed equal duties and equal pay for officials.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Asked for a progressive tax for all state and local expenditure, with indirect taxes abolished.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Wanted all political power in the people's elected representatives and armed people rather than a monarch commanding.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Condemned unearned income of property owners; held that capitalists draw wealth created by workers and that property owners as such exploit labour.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Held that big industry creates the means for abundance and freedom, making its development the basis of socialism rather than a catastrophe.

job-guarantee.rationale: His group's 1848 programme set up national workshops with the state guaranteeing a livelihood to all workers and care for those unable to work.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Said English workers share the feast of England's monopoly of the world market and the colonies, thinking like the bourgeois on colonial policy.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Wrote that the value of a product of labour is determined by the labour-time needed to produce it, as long established.

land-redistribution.rationale: Proposed taking feudal and large estates into public hands for large-scale farming for all, and putting rural proletarians in collective possession; no individual splitting.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Demanded religious bodies be private associations with no influence on public education or law.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Calls for replacing competing private producers with production run by society to a common plan; says free competition has become a fetter and causes periodic crises.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wrote that the final causes of social change are in changes of the modes of production and exchange, not in men's brains; later conceded ideas interact (Bloch).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Held that the working class can come to power only under a democratic republic and called for abolishing monarchy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Demanded complete separation of church and state, no public funds and no influence on public education for any religious body.

nation-first.rationale: Held that workers have no country, that revolution must be international, and favoured united action of workers across nations.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mixed: backed Poland, Ireland and free decision for Alsace-Lorraine, but in 1849 denied viable independence to most small Slavic peoples.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Wanted religious communities deprived of influence on public education and the school secular, though they may run their own schools privately.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Insisted on concentrating all political power in the hands of the people's representatives, criticising the powerless Reichstag.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wrote that within the family the husband is the bourgeois and the wife the proletariat, and monogamy rests on male supremacy.

people-in-arms.rationale: His 1848 programme demanded universal arming of the people so armies would be workers' armies.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Said communism deprives no one of the power to appropriate products of society for use, only of subjugating others' labour through appropriation.

positive-liberty.rationale: Held that real human freedom requires a society freed from class distinctions and anxiety over subsistence.

premarital-sex.rationale: Predicted removal of the anxiety over consequences and a more tolerant opinion of maidens' honour once property relations change.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said nationalities would mingle and dissolve under communism, and national differences are vanishing with the world market.

production-for-use.rationale: Called for production by society on a plan based on available resources and the needs of the whole society, not for private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described capital as the property that exploits wage labour and the capitalist class as appropriating wealth created by the exploited.

property-franchise.rationale: Described property qualifications as a low stage of the state and, in 1848, demanded votes for everyone at 21.

property-fundamental.rationale: Held that private property must be abolished and that its abolition is the main communist demand.

public-money-creation.rationale: Demanded that private banks be replaced by a state bank issuing legal-tender paper money and centralisation of credit in the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Demanded that railways, canals, shipping, mines and, as the state takes over trusts and joint-stock enterprises, all industry become public property.

recall-officials.rationale: Praised the Commune's election of all posts with the electors' right to recall their delegate at any time.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Praised binding mandates and recall at any time for officials and deputies as safeguard against becoming masters of society.

religion-illusion.rationale: Wrote that religion is the fantastic reflection of alien forces and will vanish when society controls its production.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Praised the Commune paying all officials only workers' wages and in 1848 demanded paid representatives so workers could sit.

restore-past-order.rationale: Opposed reactionary socialists who wanted to restore feudal and patriarchal society, calling it impossible and harmful.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Valued primitive communal society historically, but held that communism depends on advanced big industry and an expanded productive base.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: In the Manifesto credited the bourgeoisie with rescuing much of the population from the idiocy of rural life.

second-chamber.rationale: Said Germany could do very well without the federal Bundesrat chamber.

separate-church-state.rationale: Demanded complete separation of church and state, with clergy paid only by their own congregations.

separated-powers.rationale: Demanded concentration of all political power in the people's representatives rather than a balance of checking bodies.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Condemned the husband's supremacy in marriage and argued for a real common footing of rights and duties.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Endorsed the Commune's lesson that the working class cannot manage with the old state machine and must do away with its repressive machinery, while seeing peaceful change possible in democratic republics.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Said in 1847 that communist revolution cannot happen in one country alone but only in the leading civilized countries together.

socialized-care.rationale: Wrote that private housekeeping will become a social industry and care and education of children a public affair.

socialized-markets.rationale: Looked to the replacement of commodity exchange between firms by planned social production; exchange and money become superfluous.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Held that the state is in general the state of the most powerful economically dominant class and that the modern state is a capitalist machine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed more national factories, workshops, railroads and land improvement in proportion to national capital, and centralisation of credit in a state bank.

state-harmful.rationale: Said the state is not abolished but dies out after society takes the means of production; rejected abolishing it out of hand, and called it at best an inherited evil.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Criticised Dühring's ban on religion as out-Bismarcking Bismarck that would give religion martyrs and a longer life; wanted it to die out naturally.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Included heavy inheritance taxes and abolition of inheritance through collateral lines among the first measures.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Listed strongly progressive taxes and limitation of private property by progressive taxation among the first measures after a democratic victory.

taxation-theft.rationale: Advocated heavy progressive taxation and heavy inheritance taxes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: By 1875 and 1891 condemned annexations (Poles, Danes, Alsace-Lorraine) as burdens that enslave the annexer; earlier 1849 praised US conquest of California as civilising.

traditional-family.rationale: Wrote that the modern individual family rests on the open or concealed domestic slavery of the wife and that the monogamous family must cease to be society's economic unit.

unions-good.rationale: Described trade unions as unexcelled schools of war for workers and defended their strikes as the movement of a rising class.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejected every attempt to impose moral dogma as an eternal law above history, holding morality has been class morality.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rejected conspiratorial minority revolutions and said the working class must emancipate itself, though he valued theoretical leadership of the party.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Treated small property as a doomed form and opposed schemes to make workers owners of small dwellings as a bourgeois remedy; goal was common ownership.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Held that women's liberation requires bringing the whole female sex back into public industry and ending the family as economic unit.

worker-ownership.rationale: Praised the Commune's plan to combine associations of workers in each factory into one union, and urged cooperative production for peasants; his main goal was ownership by society as a whole.

workers-nation.rationale: Held that the working class is an international class whose revolution must be international; workers have no country.

workers-own-party.rationale: Wrote that as the working class matures it constitutes itself as its own party and votes for its own representatives, not capitalists'.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wanted industry run with the participation of all members of society and praised the Commune's workers' associations; no specific ballot scheme.

notes: Joint works with Marx are counted as his words. Positions changed over time: in 1849 he denied viable independence to most small Slavic peoples and praised US conquest of California, while by 1875 and 1891 he opposed annexations and backed Poland and free choice in Alsace-Lorraine; in 1895 he rejected minority revolutions in favour of mass electoral organisation while retaining the right of revolution. His Algeria (1848) articles and Ireland writings were not available to read and are not used.
